status: captured, judged by 5 AI jurors and the owner (2026-10-30)

entries.note: home page; in practice the ages 0-3 program page behind a brand splash

business.what: Therapy programs for neurodivergent people of all ages (0-3, 3-18, 18-65, 65+). Main action 'Get started' (referral). Funding not stated; the wording (Regional Center, IFSP, IPP) points to California's state-funded system, so families probably pay nothing (inference).
business.action_that_pays: 'Get started' referral; 'Donate' is the loudest button

entries.veto: Motion ignores prefers-reduced-motion entirely; after ~12.5 s idle the page navigates itself to the next program URL (also under reduced motion); process steps fade out after they pass.

claims.verdict: confirmed for feeling, contested for function
claims.evidence: 8 flat chromatic colours, 0 gradients; reads as 'not a clinic'. But the strongest orange goes to Donate, and green/yellow/white pairs fail contrast (1.82-2.78:1).

claims.verdict: confirmed for distinctiveness, contested for readability
claims.evidence: Robuck Rounded display up to 575px; the h1 'The first years matter most' runs 5 lines split over two screens. Both faces are rounded (ABC Diatype Rounded Plus 88%, Robuck Rounded 12%): rounded reads as warmth here, not as 'modern'.

claims.claim: Graphics fit the goal without modern 3D vectors
claims.evidence: Flat illustration, 0 shadows, 0 gradients, 0 blur; friendly for parents of young children. It builds warmth, not trust.

claims.claim: Scrolling is good, objects give a modern impression
claims.evidence: Well built (GSAP ScrollTrigger, SplitText, Lenis, Lottie; motion craft 8), but the motion is mostly decoration, ignores reduced motion, fades the referral steps out after they pass, and auto-navigates when idle. The objects read as a children's book, not modern.

library_candidates: Tagline as the visual system: 'see life from a different angle' becomes tilted type, tilted cards and rotated letters.
Program pages as chapters of one life journey, each with its own colour and a 'Next stop' hand-off to the next age band.
Name the visitor's worry in one sentence right before a three-step process.
Flat, subject-specific illustration (no 3D) for warmth with families.
Scroll card deck that tilts as it passes (only with a static reduced-motion layout).
avoid: Donate louder than the main action; no action on the first screen
Motion with no reduced-motion path, above all for a neurodivergent audience
Content that fades out after the visitor passes it
No proof, no cost or eligibility answer for anxious parents

entries.note: same template as the home page, page for page; count Maxima's lessons once

business.what: Same company, program page for ages 3-18; step 1 names who refers the child (Regional Center Service Coordinator).

entries.veto: As ref-0004, plus green-on-green type pairs at 1.82-2.78:1.

claims.verdict: confirmed as program coding, contested for reading
claims.evidence: Green keys the 3-18 chapter (sensible per-program colour), but 9-10 chromatic colours and 9 failing contrast pairs.
Stickers cover letters of the main headline ('YE_RS'); h1 5 lines, h3 7 lines on mobile.
Flat illustration suits young children; nothing speaks to teenagers, the same 'learn' graphic as the home page.
Same mechanism and same defects as ref-0004.

library_candidates: Per-program colour chapters inside one template, with a hand-off to the next program.
avoid: Reusing one page template so literally that the age band changes nothing but the colour

business.what: Remote 1-on-1 personal training with a human coach through an app: $50 first month, then $199/month, 30-day full refund.
business.action_that_pays: 'Find your coach' / 'Get started' / 'Start the 1-Minute Quiz' (three labels for one action)

entries.veto: Infinite card marquee with readable text that pauses only on hover (WCAG 2.2.2); the rotating headline word keeps going under reduced motion.

claims.evidence: Real members across ages, coach selfie video, member video testimonials. The hero athlete may be too fit for someone who failed to train alone.

claims.claim: Product screens let the user focus
claims.evidence: One phone, centred on black, one headline, one action; the screens show scenes from the customer's life (a travel week, moved workouts, an injury record). The marquee and rotating word compete with it.
They are photo cards with app-UI overlay chips (day pickers, watch screen), not icon cards.

claims.claim: Animation in every section is very good
claims.evidence: Measured live: restrained CSS fades (600/300 ms), header hide (200 ms), phone splash-to-app, video cards growing on scroll. Results, testimonials and footer have no scroll motion; the marquee is the weakest piece.

library_candidates: Price and refund right under the hero action ('$50 first month, then $199/month. Cancel within 30 days for a full refund.').
App screens written as small scenes from the customer's life.
Show a member's intake data (schedule, equipment, injuries, goals) to prove 'personal'.
One product screen alone on black under one headline to focus attention.
Monochrome palette so the photographs carry all colour; a light serif display for a premium voice.
Header that hides on scroll-down (200 ms) and returns on scroll-up.
avoid: Infinite marquee with readable text and no pause control
Key benefit cards cut off at the carousel edge

owner_taste_signal: Across six references the owner's scores follow distinctiveness and visual craft, not business or customer: the two pages the AI jury ranks lowest (Maxima, 4.7-5.0) get the owner's highest score (9), the page the jury ranks highest (Future, 6.9) gets 8. That is a real taste signal for art direction; it is not a judgement of whether a page works for its business.
